'''Sundari''' was the [[Domed city/Legends|domed]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] faction of [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]], located on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], where it stood alongside Mandalore's traditional capital of [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]]. Situated within one of Mandalore's [[white]]-sand [[Desert/Legends|desert]] regions, the [[Bio-cube/Legends|bio-cube]] city of Sundari hosted a large number of New Mandalorians by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], including the sect's leader, [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]]. [[Hover taxi/Legends|Automated transports]] ferried individuals from the city's [[Sundari shipping docks/Legends|docks]] into its interior, which was filled with high-technology structures made of [[Permacrete/Legends|permacrete]], [[Beskar/Legends|''beskar'']] [[Iron/Legends|iron]], and [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]]. Sundari was guarded by its dedicated [[Mandalorian Guard/Legends|police force]], and the city's [[Skylane/Legends|skylanes]] were patrolled by their [[Buirk'alor-class airspeeder|''Buirk'alor''-class airspeeders]].

During the early stages of the [[Cloning/Legends|Clone]] Wars, Sundari's [[Memorial Shrine/Legends|Memorial Shrine]] was the target of a [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] [[Attack on the Memorial Shrine/Legends|attack]], orchestrated by the radical and violent Mandalorian splinter group known as the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]]. Some time later, the city was struck by an epidemic of [[Poison/Legends|poisonings]] among its [[Youngling/Legends|youth]], the source of which was traced to a shipment of tainted [[Tea/Legends|tea]] delivered to Sundari by a contingent of [[Moogan/Legends|Moogan]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]]. This incident was part of a larger trend of [[Mandalorian black market conspiracy/Legends|corruption]] among its government's officials, leading to the arrest of New Mandalorian [[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]] [[Almec/Legends|Almec]] for his role in allowing the [[Black market/Legends|black market]] to operate on Mandalore, and his subsequent incarceration in a [[Royal prison/Legends|Sundari prison]].

Two [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, in [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], Sundari was the primary target of the Death Watch's [[Takeover of Mandalore/Legends|coup]] against the New Mandalorian regime. Having entered into an alliance with the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] and assembled an [[Army/Legends|army]] of criminals known as the [[Shadow Collective/Legends|Shadow Collective]], Death Watch played the role of heroic saviors combating the ordered onslaught of the Collective's [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]] who, in secret, terrorized Sundari at [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Maul's command, in order to prove the New Mandalorian [[Ruling Council (New Mandalorians)/Legends|government]] an ineffective body. Winning the favor of the public by protecting Sundari's populous when Duchess Satine Kryze and her administration could not, Death Watch deposed the duchess, while their leader, [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], replaced Kryze as the [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|ruler]] of the New Mandalorians. However, Vizsla's command was usurped shortly thereafter by Darth Maul, causing a divide in the ranks of Death Watch between [[Mandalorian super commando/Legends|those]] who pledged their loyalty to the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], and [[Nite Owls/Legends|those]] who followed Vizsla's former [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] [[Bo-Katan Kryze/Legends|Bo-Katan Kryze]] and refused to recognize the rule of a non-Mandalorian, eventually leading to a vicious [[Battle of Mandalore/Legends|battle]] on the outskirts of Sundari between the two factions.

==Description==
Nestled within a vast, [[black]]-[[Color/Legends|colored]] [[Domed city/Legends|dome]]<ref name="TMP" /> that protected against the inhospitable [[Desert/Legends|desert]]<ref name="MandaloreEncyclopedia">{{SWE|locations|mandalore|Mandalore}}</ref> region of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] in which it was located,<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> Sundari was a large [[Bio-cube/Legends|bio-cube]] [[City/Legends|city]],<ref name="MandaloreEncyclopedia" /> and the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] city of the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] faction.<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> Sundari enclosed one of Mandalore's largest active [[Mining/Legends|mines]] of [[Beskar/Legends|''beskar'']] [[Iron/Legends|iron]] [[Ore/Legends|ore]] within its outer walls, providing the city with valuable resources and a major strategic asset.<ref name="FLT">''[[Friends Like These]]''</ref> It was surrounded by a number of other cube cities, smaller in size than the large black dome,<ref name="TMP" /> and constructed by the New Mandalorians to survive the harsh conditions of Mandalore's deserts.<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> On its outer face, Sundari hosted [[Sundari shipping docks/Legends|shipping docks]] for receiving supply shipments to the city,<ref name="Corruption" /> and welcoming visiting [[Starship/Legends|starships]];<ref name="Academy" /> [[Hover taxi/Legends|automated transports]] waited to ferry beings from the docks into the city's interior, and [[Officer/Legends|officers]] of the [[Mandalorian Guard/Legends|Mandalorian police]] force patrolled the area.<ref name="TMP" />

[[File:Peace_Park.png|thumb|left|300px|The [[Peace Park/Legends|Peace Park]] at the heart of Sundari]]
Inside Sundari's black dome, the city was comprised of a complex series of rectangular and often cube-shaped buildings, constructed in close quarters with large blocks of [[Permacrete/Legends|permacrete]] and ''beskar'' [[Iron/Legends|iron]], with sheets of [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]]<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> that ranged from translucent to transparent.<ref name="TMP" /> Its high-technology structures<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> rose up from the ground and hung from the dome's vaulted ceiling, alike,<ref name="Academy" /> maximizing the space available.<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> [[Skylane/Legends|Skylanes]] filled with [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeders]] wove between Sundari's glass towers,<ref name="TMP" /> patrolled by [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police]]-owned [[Buirk'alor-class airspeeder|''Buirk'alor''-class]] [[Speeder/Legends|speeders]].<ref name="TCWIV">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]''</ref> Near the [[Heart/Legends|heart]] of the city stood the [[Sundari Royal Palace/Legends|Sundari Royal Palace]],<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> home to Sundari's [[Ruling Council (New Mandalorians)/Legends|leaders]],<ref name="Corruption" /> and the tranquil [[Peace Park/Legends|Peace Park]] that housed the [[Memorial Shrine/Legends|Memorial Shrine]].<ref name="TMP" /> Peace Park was one of several places dedicated to the natural greenery Sundari's external desert surroundings denied its people, ranging from plazas to rooftop [[Garden/Legends|gardens]], but the city's vegetation was highly regimented, with everything from [[Bush/Legends|shrubbery]] to [[Tree/Legends|trees]] meticulously tended and trimmed from their natural forms into stark geometric shapes.<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" />

Sundari's most promising [[Youngling/Legends|youths]] received an education at the [[Royal Academy of Government/Legends|Royal Academy of Government]], which prepared them for leadership roles in the New Mandalorian government,<ref name="Academy" /> while other New Mandalorian children attended a [[Sundari Mandalorian school/Legends|different school]] within the city.<ref name="Corruption" /> Among Sundari's financial establishments stood the [[Mandalore Banking Center/Legends|Mandalore Banking Center]],<ref name="SoREpGuide" /> a multistory facility housing wealth-laden vaults. The city boasted its own judiciary courts, and Sundari's convicted criminals<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> were held in a [[Royal prison/Legends|prison]] that stretched downward from Sundari's domed heights.<ref name="Academy" /> The [[Sundari Peace Museum]] housed [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]] on display.<ref name="GotCK" /> By the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> a new [[Sundari Mandalorian hospital/Legends|hospital]] was opened in the city, with facilities to treat hundreds of patients, and an outdoor grounds large enough to accommodate several<ref name="Corruption" /> [[Aka'jor-class shuttle/Legends|''Aka'jor''-class shuttles]]<ref name="TCWIV" /> loaded with individuals in need of medical treatment.<ref name="Corruption" />

==History==
===Early history===
In [[738 BBY]],<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> following a significant growth in [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] militancy that alarmed the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and its [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] protectors, a brief and targeted conflict<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> that came to be known as the [[Mandalorian Excision]] broke out between the Republic and the Mandalorians, bringing devastation to several worlds within [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalorian space]]. Along with swaths of [[Fenel]], [[Ordo/Legends|Ordo]], and [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]],<ref name="TEGW" /> portions of Mandalore were transformed into deserts of white sand,<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> while the Mandalorians were disarmed and their planet occupied by Republic forces for [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]]. From the caretaker government that the Republic left in charge of Mandalore in the aftermath of the Excision, arose the New Mandalorian faction;<ref name="TEGW" /> a reformist [[Politics/Legends|political]] group, the New Mandalorians renounced violence and the [[Canons of Honor|warrior codes]] of Mandalore's past, while preaching peace, neutrality, and tolerance.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Sundari_Desert.png|thumb|right|300px|Sundari was founded in the deserts of Mandalore left behind by the [[Mandalorian Excision]].]]
The New Mandalorians used their talents as builders and inventors to create grand<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> bio-cube cities<ref name="MandaloreEncyclopedia" /> in Mandalore's desert wastes,<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> forging a new society isolated from Mandalore's [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]] clans.<ref name="TEA" /> They constructed the domed city of Sundari around one of Mandalore's largest active ''beskar'' mines,<ref name="FLT" /> and claimed it as their faction's capital,<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> in opposition to [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]],<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> Mandalore's traditional capital that had stood since before the [[Mandalorian Wars]], thousands of years prior.<ref name="TEA" /> The New Mandalorians' dedication to peace, their love of advanced technology,<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> and the ''beskar'' mines of Sundari,<ref name="FLT" /> allowed for them to claim ascendancy over the disorganized warrior clans on Mandalore for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]],<ref name="TEA" /> leading the Republic to officially recognize Sundari as the capital of Mandalore<ref name="Corruption" /> over Keldabe,<ref name="O66" /> as Mandalore gained [[Senator/Legends|representation]] in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]].<ref name="VoT">{{TCW|Voyage of Temptation}}</ref> The city came under the protection of the Mandalorian police, as well as units of the [[Mandalorian Royal Guard/Legends|Mandalorian Royal Guard]].<ref name="Guard">{{SWE|groups|mandalorianguard|Mandalorian Guard}}</ref>

===The Clone Wars===
Around 22 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]],<ref name="TERC" /> in the midst of the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-spanning conflict between the Galactic Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] known as the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="TEGW" /> [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] journeyed to Sundari on behalf of the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] in order to ascertain the truth behind rumors claiming that Mandalore—a staunch political ally of the Republic<ref name="TMP" /> since the rise of the New Mandalorians in the wake of the Mandalorian Excision<ref name="TEGW" />—was secretly assembling an [[Army/Legends|army]] for the Separatists of the Confederacy. When he touched down at the Sundari docks, Kenobi was taken by automated [[Transport/Legends|transport]] to the royal palace, where he met with the New Mandalorians' [[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]], [[Almec/Legends|Almec]], and their leader, [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]]<ref name="TMP" /> of the neighboring world, [[Kalevala/Legends|Kalevala]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:PeacePark-TMP.png|thumb|left|300px|Peace Park, shortly before falling victim to a terrorist attack]]
While taking a walk with Kryze in the nearby Peace Park, Kenobi witnessed a [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] [[Attack on the Memorial Shrine/Legends|Bombing of the Memorial Shrine]] housed at the park, by a [[Death Watch bomber/Legends|member]] of the violent Mandalorian splinter group known as the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]]. Kenobi attempted to apprehend the bomber, taking part in a lengthy chase that ended at a dead-end balcony; after a short struggle, the bomber [[Death/Legends|took his own life]] by leaping from the balcony's edge. Together with Duchess Kryze, Kenobi accompanied the deceased [[Gender/Legends|man's]] body to his home of [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]],<ref name="TMP" /> one of Mandalore's two [[Moon/Legends|moons]],<ref name="TEA" /> where he discovered the [[Death Watch hideout|hideout]] of the Death Watch among the [[Concordian mines/Legends|''beskar'' mines]] that had been previously thought abandoned.<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> Kenobi and Kryze escaped a [[Fight on Concordia/Legends|skirmish]] with the Death Watch's [[Troop/Legends|troops]], returning to Sundari where they boarded the Duchess' personal [[Yacht/Legends|star yacht]],<ref name="TMP" /> the [[Coronet/Legends|''Coronet'']],<ref name="VoT" /> bound for [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to explain the truth of current Mandalorian affairs to the Republic senate. While Kryze spoke before the Galactic Senate, a [[Unidentified New Mandalorian scout/Legends|New Mandalorian scout]] reported to Prime Minister Almec in Sundari, informing him of the army Death Watch had amassed on Concordia. Before they could mobilize an attack, however, Death Watch's leader, [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], was ordered to stand down by his ally and benefactor, [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] of the Confederacy of Independent [[Star system/Legends|Systems]].<ref name="DoM">{{TCW|Duchess of Mandalore}}</ref>

Following Duchess Kryze's proclamation that Mandalore would remain a neutral entity in the [[Cloning/Legends|Clone]] Wars, Republic funded [[Hyperspace route/Legends|trade routes]]<ref name="Corruption" /> to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] world<ref name="TEA" /> were largely severed, and re-prioritized elsewhere.<ref name="Corruption" /> Having cut themselves off<ref name="TEA" /> from Mandalore's [[Farm/Legends|farming]] communities in the parts of Mandalore<ref name="O66" /> unspoiled by the Mandalorian Excision,<ref name="TEGW" /> Sundari began to suffer from food shortages without Republic aid, leaving many of its residents starving.<ref name="Corruption" /> To remedy the dire situation, Prime Minister Almec took it upon himself to [[Mandalorian black market conspiracy/Legends|establish]] a [[Black market/Legends|black market]] trade network in secret, in order to get food to the New Mandalorian people.<ref name="Academy" />

[[File:Sundari_Hospital.png|thumb|right|185px|A newly constructed [[Sundari Mandalorian hospital/Legends|Sundari hospital]]]]
The illegal intake of supplies to Sundari came at a dangerous cost: [[Moogan/Legends|Moogan]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] arrived in Sundari, [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|bribing]] their way passed a [[Unidentified Mandalorian customs official/Legends|customs official]] in order to unload shipments of [[Ardees Beverage/Legends|Ardees Beverage tea]]. Seeking to increase their total profits from the shipment, the Moogans diluted the [[Tea/Legends|tea]] with the chemical [[Slabin/Legends|slabin]] from a [[Sundari dock warehouse/Legends|warehouse]] at Sundari's docks, but instead of a harmless mixture, the slabin dosage was incorrectly calculated, contaminating the tea. The tea was distributed to a number of New Mandalorian [[school]]s, resulting in hundreds of children becoming violently ill, and many were taken to a recently opened [[Medcenter/Legends|hospital]] in the city. The hospital was set to be toured that [[Standard day/Legends|day]] by Duchess Kryze and her offworld guest, Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], and upon discovering the outbreak of [[Poison/Legends|poisoned]] youths, Kryze and Amidala set out to discover the source of the illness plaguing Sundari's schoolchildren. Upon visiting one school that had been affected, the two politicians discovered the [[Ardees Beverage Company/Legends|Ardees]] bottled tea to be the source of the poison, and traced the shipment back to the Sundari warehouse from which the Moogan smugglers were operating out of. Following a [[Skirmish at the Sundari docks|brief shootout]] between the smugglers and several officers of the Mandalorian guard, the operation was dismantled and an antidote was provided to the hospitalized children.<ref name="Corruption" />

The corruption that Kryze and Amidala exposed among Sundari's officials—with the [[Unidentified Sundari school superintendent/Legends|superintendent]] of a school afflicted by the poisoned tea, and the [[Siddiq/Legends|head]] of the [[Unidentified Mandalorian shipping company/Legends|shipping company]] responsible for dealing with the [[Mooga/Legends|Moogans]] among the guilty<ref name="Corruption" />—the New Mandalorian Duchess requested a member of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] come to Mandalore in order to help stop the black market trade network, and lecture against the perils of corruption at the Royal Academy of Government. Agreeing to the request, the Jedi Council dispatched Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] to Mandalore; Tano landed at the Sundari docks with [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|her master]]<ref name="Academy" /> and a detachment of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clones]] from the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]].<ref name="TCWIV" /> Though her master and the clones departed Sundari shortly in order to return to the war, Tano was welcomed to the city by Kryze, Prime Minister Almec, and a group of [[Cadet/Legends|cadets]] from the Academy.<ref name="Academy" />

[[File:Royal_Academy_of_Government.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Sundari's [[Royal Academy of Government/Legends|Royal Academy of Government]]]]
For two days, Tano lectured at Sundari's Royal Academy, speaking on the subject of corruption among government leadership, and the duty of the common citizen to ensure lawful behavior among society's rulers. Taking the Jedi's words to heart, a group of cadets aware of Sundari's food shortages, decided to investigate the city's [[Sundari warehouse district/Legends|warehouse district]] for signs of improper conduct. There, the children discovered a [[Government warehouse/Legends|government warehouse]] being used to store black market goods, and a group of smugglers meeting with Prime Minister Almec. Fearing the repercussions of his discovery, Almec moved against the cadets and had them arrested by the [[Mandalorian secret service/Legends|New Mandalorian Secret Service]], in addition to Duchess Kryze, who had been informed by her cadet nephew [[Korkie Kryze/Legends|Korkie]] of their findings. Almec [[Prisoner/Legends|incarcerated]] the Duchess and the students in a Sundari [[Prison/Legends|prison]], only for Padawan Ahsoka Tano to mount a rescue that resulted in Kryze and the students being freed, while Almec and his conspirators were jailed for their crimes,<ref name="Academy" /> found guilty on charges of corruption by Sundari's courts.<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> With the black market network shut down and its orchestrator in prison, Tano departed Sundari to return to her duties under her [[Jedi Master/Legends|master]].<ref name="Academy" />

Later in the war, Sundari hosted a [[Confederate–Republic peace conference/Legends|conference]] at the royal palace, between a delegation from the Republic and Confederacy of Independent Systems seeking a peaceful end to the Clone Wars. Proceedings broke down, though, when the disenfranchised Separatist [[Separatist Senate/Legends|senator]] [[Lux Bonteri/Legends|Lux Bonteri]] stormed into Duchess Kryze's throne room accusing the Confederate [[Head of State/Legends|leader]] Count Dooku of murdering his [[Parent/Legends|mother]], [[Mina Bonteri/Legends|Mina Bonteri]]. The young Bonteri was forcibly removed from the hall by a cadre of Separatist [[BX-series droid commando/Legends|BX-series droid commandos]], and taken to the Confederacy's [[C-9979 landing craft/Legends|C-9979 landing craft]] at the Sundari docks where he would have been killed were it not for the intervention of [[Togruta/Legends|Togruta]] Padawan Ahsoka Tano, who had returned to Mandalore as part of a security detail for the Republic's [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomats]]. Tano rescued Bonteri, and fled Sundari aboard a [[Phoenix (GX1 short hauler)/Legends|Republic vessel]].<ref name="AFiN">{{TCW|A Friend in Need}}</ref>

====Downfall of the New Mandalorians====
{{Quote|I will use my army of crime lords to attack different targets across Sundari, and sow chaos to undermine the Duchess's rule. Our gangsters will make her look too weak to maintain control. Then you and your Death Watch will capture and arrest us, bringing order where Satine's weak government cannot.''"<br />"''We'll be saviors.''"<br />"''Exactly.|[[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] and [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]]|<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" />}}
[[File:Moj-TakeoverOnMandalore.png|thumb|right|300px|The [[Shadow Collective/Legends|Shadow Collective's]] [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] soldiers rampage through Sundari]]
In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="Date">According to the novel ''[[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy]]'', the events of the takeover on Mandalore occur two years after those seen in the Mandalorian episode trilogy from the first season of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''—"[[The Mandalore Plot]]," "[[Voyage of Temptation]]," and "[[Duchess of Mandalore]]." These episodes are noted to take place in the year [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] by ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''.</ref> Sundari and other New Mandalorian territories on Mandalore came [[Takeover of Mandalore/Legends|under attack]] by the [[Shadow Collective/Legends|Shadow Collective]], an assembly of criminals drawn from [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]], the [[Spice/Legends|spice]]-[[Drug dealer|dealing]] [[Pyke Syndicate/Legends|Pyke Syndicate]], and the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartels]]. These offworld [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]] were secretly in collusion with the Death Watch as their leader, the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], had forged an alliance with Death Watch [[Commander/Legends|commander]] Pre [[Clan Vizsla/Legends|Vizsla]] to topple the New Mandalorians' pacifist regime. As part of a plan to exemplify the ineffectiveness of the New Mandalorian administration, the Collective's thugs rampaged throughout Sundari, overwhelming a police force that proved incapable of defending against the aggressors. Sundari's docks fell quickly into Collective control, while [[Pyke/Legends|Pyke]] gangsters assaulted the<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> Mandalore [[Bank/Legends|Banking]] Center,<ref name="SoREpGuide" /> and [[Black Sun foot soldier/Legends|Black Sun foot soldiers]] opened [[Blaster/Legends|fire]] on the Peace Park with reckless abandon, killing civilian and [[Police officer/Legends|police officers]] alike.<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> Panicked, the people of Sundari gathered at the Royal Palace to demand action from their leaders, only to be advised to remain calm and cautioned to keep to their peaceful principles by Duchess Satine Kryze. It was then that Death Watch appeared, swooping down on the Sundari palace via [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]], as Pre Vizsla pledged to do what Kryze could not: defend the New Mandalorians against the crime syndicates and keep Sundari safe.<ref name="SoR">{{TCW|Shades of Reason}}</ref>

Across Sundari, Death Watch's soldiers engaged the Shadow Collective's criminals in staged battles; the Collective had played the role of villains to be vanquished by the Death Watch well,<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> and as the Mandalorian warriors triumphed over the offworld gangsters, the populous of Sundari applauded their efforts and lauded the Death Watch as saviors. At the docks of Sundari, Death Watch troops subdued the Black Sun and Pyke forces holding the dock workers captive, freeing the grateful New Mandalorians and taking the criminals into custody.<ref name="SoR" /> In Peace Park, Pre Vizsla's loyal [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] [[Bo-Katan Kryze/Legends|Bo-Katan]] and her handpicked [[Squad/Legends|unit]] known as the [[Nite Owls/Legends|Nite Owls]]<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> rescued a number of New Mandalorian children from Black Sun footsoldiers, [[Whipcord launcher/Legends|binding]] the gangsters with [[Fibercord/Legends|fibercord]], while Vizsla himself apprehended a team of Pyke thugs led by [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Maul's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]], [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]], as they attempted to flee the pilfered<ref name="SoR" /> Mandalore Banking Center.<ref name="SoREpGuide" /> With the backing of the New Mandalorian people now firmly his, Pre Vizsla stormed the Sundari Royal Palace with a cadre of Death Watch soldiers, deposing and imprisoning Duchess Kryze and her supporters, while proclaiming himself the new Prime Minister<ref name="SoR" /> and [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']],<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> the traditional leader of the Mandalorians.<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref>

[[File:AlmecDeathWatch-ShadesOfReason.png|thumb|left|300px|Sundari falls under [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] control, with Prime Minister [[Almec/Legends|Almec]] serving as the public face of their regime]]
With Vizsla's own ambitions met, he betrayed his [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] allies and had both Maul and Opress jailed. Yet Maul had suspected that Vizsla would turn on them once he had what he desired, and planned accordingly, allowing himself to be taken into custody in order to find a more malleable candidate with which to replace Vizsla among the political prisoners Death Watch had arrested.<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> Breaking free of their cell using the Force, Maul and his apprentice came upon the incarcerated former Prime Minister Almec and struck a deal with the disgraced New Mandalorian leader. The two Sith freed themselves from their confines and stormed the Royal Palace, where Maul challenged Vizsla for the right of leadership<ref name="SoR" /> under the ancient Mandalorian codes Death Watch sought to resurrect.<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> Vizsla and Maul engaged in a furious bout of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|single combat]] from which Maul emerged victorious, [[Sai cha/Legends|slaying]] Vizsla and claiming the right to lead. Almec was instituted as the new Prime Minister—a puppet ruler and the public face for Maul's new rule—while Death Watch fragmented between those who bowed to their new Sith leader, and those who refused to obey a non-Mandalorian. The Death Watch rebels rallied behind Pre Vizsla's lieutenant, Bo-Katan, and fled the Royal Palace amid a heated [[Lightfight|firefight]] with their former comrades. With his new authority, Almec appeared before the people of Sundari to announce his reinstatement and the death of Pre Vizsla, blaming the deposed Duchess Kryze for his murder, before assuring the New Mandalorians that Vizsla's goals of remilitarization would live on.<ref name="SoR" />

[[Standard week/Legends|Weeks]] after she had been imprisoned, Duchess Kryze was rescued from jail by Bo-Katan and a team of her rebellious Death Watch, along with Kryze's nephew Korkie and [[Lagos/Legends|several]] of his [[Soniee/Legends|school]] [[Amis/Legends|friends]]. The group attempted to escort the deposed duchess out of Sundari, but were pursued and attacked by units of [[Mandalorian super commando/Legends|Mandalorian super commandos]] loyal to Darth Maul. Kryze's defenders were defeated and she was recaptured, though not before she could transmit a message to the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on Coruscant, alerting Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi to the state of affairs plaguing Sundari. Intent to rescue his one time lover, Kenobi traveled to Sundari alone, in disguise and aboard a [[Twilight/Legends|borrowed]] [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]]; he succeeded in sneaking Kryze from her prison confines, but his escape attempts never made it beyond Sundari's docks. Kenobi's ship was destroyed and he was captured alongside Kryze, taken back to the Royal Palace where Kryze was [[Shiak|killed]] before his [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] by Darth Maul<ref name="Lawless">{{TCW|The Lawless}}</ref> as revenge for the wounds Kenobi inflicted upon the [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] Sith Lord nearly a decade prior.<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> Kenobi was subsequently taken from the palace and bound for Sundari's prison, as Maul preferred to let the Jedi live with his anguish rather than kill him outright.<ref name="Lawless" />

[[File:BattleOfSundari-shippingdocks.png|thumb|right|300px|Heavy [[Battle of Mandalore/Legends|fighting]] broke out between the two Death Watch factions, consuming [[Sundari shipping docks/Legends|Sundari's docks]]]]
Before Kenobi could reach the cell he had been bound for, his captors were ambushed by Bo-Katan and her forces, who quickly killed the Sith loyalists and freed Kenobi, intent on getting the Jedi Master out of Sundari. The group raced through Sundari's skylanes with their jetpacks—even Kenobi, who had been gifted a spare by Bo-Katan upon his rescue—fighting off pursuers on the way to Sundari's docks, where they found [[Battle of Mandalore/Legends|open conflict]] raging between the two factions of the Death Watch, those loyal to Maul and those loyal to Bo-Katan. Fighting their way through the larger hostilities, Bo-Katan called down a<ref name="Lawless" /> [[Kom'rk-class fighter/transport/Legends|''Kom'rk''-class fighter/transport]]<ref name="TCWIV" /> to evacuate Kenobi. While she stayed to continue the fight, the Jedi Master was taken from Sundari, and off of Mandalore.<ref name="Lawless" />

At the same time war raged between the fractured Death Watch, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] arrived in Sundari, having [[Force sense/Legends|sensed]] the whereabouts of his former apprentice, Darth Maul. Journeying to the Royal Palace, Sidious confronted Maul and his own apprentice, Savage Opress, over a breach of the [[Order of the Sith Lords|Sith Order's]] [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]]. The three [[darksider]]s became embroiled in a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] that raged through the palace throne room, out onto a balcony overlooking Sundari, and then down into the square below. During the fighting Opress was killed, and the duel came to an end soon after as Maul was overpowered by his former master and subdued with the power of [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]]. However, Sidious elected not to kill the defeated Maul, preferring to keep him alive for his own future purposes.<ref name="Lawless" />

===Imperial occupation===
As the Clone Wars came to an end, the Galactic Republic was [[Declaration of a New Order|transformed]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], under the newly crowned [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine.<ref name="RotS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Though the new Empire's relationship with Mandalore was cordial at first—offering large sums for mining rights in the ''beskar''-rich [[Tokursh]] region of the planet, and brokering starship contracts with the [[MandalMotors/Legends|MandalMotors]] company<ref name="ImpCom501st">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref>—the Imperial grip on the Mandalorian homeworld later tightened harshly.<ref name="HotM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> Aided by elements of the reborn Death Watch,<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> the Empire took control of Mandalore, including the city of Sundari, and operated an [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]] on the subjugated world.<ref name="FLT" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Hoping to alleviate some of the tensions rising in the capital city of Sundari, Satine has called upon her friend Padmé Amidala to make a diplomatic visit.|Newsreel for "[[Corruption (episode)|Corruption]]"|<ref name="Corruption" />}}
Sundari was first introduced to ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the [[2009]] ''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' reference book. The city subsequently appeared in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]] episode, "[[The Mandalore Plot]]," the newsreel of the following episode "[[Voyage of Temptation]]," and again in the "[[Duchess of Mandalore]]." The series' [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]] episodes "[[Corruption (episode)|Corruption]]" and "[[The Academy]]" again featured Sundari, as did the [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|fourth season]] episode "[[A Friend in Need]]." ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''{{'s}} [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth season]] marked another return to Sundari, as the city appeared in the episodes "[[Shades of Reason]]" and "[[The Lawless]]," as well as the young reader adaptation of those episodes, ''[[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy]]''.

The city of Sundari shares its name with the [[Mining/Legends|mining]] planet [[Sundari (planet)|Sundari]], first introduced to the ''Star Wars'' universe in the ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' story ''[[Turning Point (Charlene Newcomb)|Turning Point]]'', [[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Charlene Newcomb]] and published [[February 1]], [[1995]].<ref name="Turning Point Charlene Newcomb">{{JournalCite|5|Turning Point (Charlene Newcomb)}}</ref>

Since the release of ''The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' reference book,<ref name="The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars">''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''</ref> the ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' series has referred to Sundari as the capital of the planet Mandalore,<ref name="TMPEpGuide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode212.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: The Mandalore Plot}}</ref> a role previously filled by the city of Keldabe,<ref name="O66" /> since the release of the [[Star Wars (1977) 68|sixty-eighth issue]] of [[Marvel Comics|Marvel's]] [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]] in [[February]] of [[1983]].<ref name="Star Wars 1977 68">[[Star Wars (1977) 68|''Star Wars'' (1977) 68]]</ref> With the release of ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]], Keldabe was again named as the capital of Mandalore, while the pacifist Mandalorians that appeared in the television show were [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] to be members of the New Mandalorian faction,<ref name="TEA" /> with Sundari explicitly deemed the capital of their political faction, per Fry's later young reader novel, ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy''.<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> The [[Dorling Kindersley|DK]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: What Is a Sith Warrior?]]'' by [[Glenn Dakin]] confused the two Mandalorian capitals, mistaking Keldabe for Sundari, while discussing the Bombing of the Memorial Shrine.<ref name="WiaSW">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: What Is a Sith Warrior?]]''</ref>
